statements: The Interpretation and Legislative Reform (Scotland) Act 2010 does not apply to the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009, because section 1(1)(a) of the 2010 Act applies Part 1 only to Acts of the Scottish Parliament whose Bills received Royal Assent on or after the day Part 1 came into force, and the 2009 Act preceded that day.

Interpretation of the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009 is instead governed by the Scotland Act 1998 (Transitory and Transitional Provisions) (Publication and Interpretation etc. of Acts of the Scottish Parliament) Order 1999.
Schedule 2 to that 1999 Order defines "month" as meaning a calendar month.

A provision such as section 35ZA being inserted into the 2009 Act by a later Act does not bring the 2010 Act into play, because the 2010 Act keys its application to the Royal Assent date of the Act being interpreted, not to the date a provision within it was inserted.
